messages:
Sarah K.: Quick follow-up to last week's RFC — proposing we split model onboarding into a lightweight 'fast-gate' (smoke + fingerprint checks) and a later 'deep-audit' (full bench + stability) to reduce friction for small models and make retries deterministic. Thoughts?
Devin M.: +1 on split. main risk is duplicated codepaths and divergent signal meaning. how do we keep metrics consistent across both stages?
Mike L.: Agree with Devin. We should standardize a minimal canonical artifact that both stages consume (fingerprint, token-distribution, sample-output). then metrics are computed from that artifact.
Jen P.: Practical Q: for Hosted vs Dedicated customers do both stages run the same way? deep-audit is expensive (hours). we can't block onboarding for low-risk users.
Sarah K.: Good call. Proposal: fast-gate is mandatory for all. deep-audit is opt-in for dev mode / required for Dedicated and Private (policy flag). default for Hosted: schedule deep-audit async with a soft SLA (48h).
Amar R.: How do we implement async without giving false negatives? If deep-audit fails after prod rollout that's scary. need canary/fallback policy.
Devin M.: Right — we need rollout hooks. Suggest: when fast-gate passes, allow a limited canary (10% traffic) until deep-audit completes. If deep-audit fails, auto-roll back to pinned baseline and notify owner + ops.
Mike L.: That feels safe. Also: what about quantized variants? fast-gate should be aware of quantization artifacts (e.g., topk divergence). maybe a tiny quantized delta-check during fast-gate.
Jen P.: For runtime compatibility checks (KV cache, attention variants) we need a small reproducer harness that runs on target runtime (cpu/gpu/quant). keep it < 2m execution time for fast-gate.
Sarah K.: Exactly. fast-gate tests: signature compatibility, simple perf smoke (<2m), small baseline-quality delta (<5% metric drop on golden inputs), fingerprint check. deep-audit tests: full bench suite, long-run stability, stress, variance sampling, regression evals.
Devin M.: Can we sketch the contract between onboarding and runtime teams? minimal schema suggestions:
```yaml
artifact_version: "1"
fingerprint:
  sha256: "..."
metadata:
  model_arch: "decoder-only"
  tokenizer: "bpe-v3"
stage_signals:
  fast_gate: ["signature","fingerprint","mini-bench"]
  deep_audit: ["bench-suite","stability","stress-test"]
```
Mike L.: That YAML looks fine. Important: include a small `runtime_compat` block listing required ops and optional fallbacks so runtime can respond with precise incompatibility reasons.
Jen P.: Ops list idea is great. We should also include a schema version and strict validation so we can evolve without breaking older artifacts.
Amar R.: Operational tradeoff: deep-audit storage. full benches produce large outputs. proposal: keep only drift summaries in registry, and archive raw bench traces in cold storage for 90d. saves DB cost.
Sarah K.: Agreed — store summaries (p95, p99, token-cost, variance) and pointers to archived traces. Also tag audit results with rollout-id so we can correlate.
Devin M.: One more: signal alignment. fast-gate mini-bench uses 5 golden prompts. deep-audit uses 5k. need mapping so small sample predictions can be projected to full benchmark; otherwise we get mismatched alerts. maybe a calibration step per model family.
Mike L.: Calibration makes sense. We can maintain per-family regression models (cheap) to map mini-sample deltas to expected full-bench delta. update monthly or when family distribution shifts.
Jen P.: UX for model owners: show a clear timeline: fast-gate pass -> canary start -> deep-audit queued (ETA) -> final signoff or rollback. transparently show reasons for rollback with diffs.
Sarah K.: I'll draft a follow-up RFC that includes: pipeline stages, artifact schema, runtime compatibility block, canary policy, storage retention, and calibration plan. tagging this as 'implementation-ready' after review.
Amar R.: +1. small ask: include a checklist for on-call responders (what to look for when audit fails post-rollout).
Devin M.: I'll add a telemetry contract: which metrics to emit for each stage and recommended alert thresholds.

Sarah K.: thanks — will circulate draft tomorrow morning. any last quick objections?
Mike L.: no objections. excited to see the draft. :thumbsup:
Jen P.: no blockers from infra.
Devin M.: none from me.
Amar R.: all good.
Sarah K.: awesome. closing thread — will post RFC link when ready. :rocket:
